full_judgment:
3. This affected the properties of the appellant, namely, C.S. Plot Nos. 12446, 12447, 12448, appertaining to Khatian Nos. 3160, 3134 and 3153 in Mouza 94 Palaspole, P.S. Satkhira, District Khulna and two-storied building with shop in the ground floor of one of the buildings. The appellant claimed that the properties being situated outside the hat and bazar could not be treated as part of the same and taken over by the Government. Since his purchase from one Haridas Datta in 1951 the appellant had been possessing and enjoying the land with structures thereon. He renovated, extended and modernised the existing shop and constructed first floor on the other building. The appellant paid rent to the Government upto 1367 B.S. but since then the office of the Government Acquired Estate where he tendered rent was not accepting it. Previous to the acquisition of rent receiving interests the appellant had also been paying rent. Appellant asserted that the aforesaid plots are situated far away from plot No. 12408, of Khatian No. 3031-3 in Mouza Palaspole, covering an area of 2.2 acres which has been recorded as hat and bazar in the settlement records and other records of right No other plot has been shown as hat or bazar in any Khatian or any settlement record. His plots are separated from plot No. 12408 by two blocks of land and road. He made representations to the authority against inclusion of his lands as hat and bazar which were of no avail. 

 4. On behalf of the Government it was stated that the properties in question were situated within the periphery of the hat and bazar locally called Sultanpur bazar, Further, the plots and structures were acquired by the Government under sections 3(1) and 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, by a General Notification issued on April 2, 1956. The right and title of the land vested in the Government with effect from April 14, 1962. It might be that the local Tahshildar realised rent from the appellant and granted him provisional rent receipts but they did not create any right and title of the appellant. Plot Nos. 12446, 12447 and 12448 are definitely situated within the periphery of Sultanpur bazar and were, therefore not retainable class of land under section 20(2) of the Act read with Ordinance No. 12 of 1960. 

 "The land with structures on plot Nos. 12446, 12447 and 1244 is definitely situated within the periphery of Sultanpur bazar within the meaning of section 2(12) of the said Act and it is not a retain able class of land under section 20(2) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 read with Ordinance No. 12 of 1960." 

 7. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the High Court Division the appellant moved this Court and obtained leave to consider whether the properties in question being situated within the periphery of the hat and bazar as claimed by the respondents came within the meaning of hat and bazar under section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and whether word 'periphery' would include the properties in question as being within the hat and bazar. 

 8. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, learned Counsel for the appellant, submitted that since the respondents claimed to have recorded only plot No. 12408 as, bat and bazar and the appellant's lands were not shown as hat and bazar, his lands were mentioned to be within the 'periphery' of Sultanpur bazar, the learned Judges Were wrong in giving an extended meaning to the word 'periphery' and in holding that the lands in question were within Sultanpur bazar, He mentioned that the learned Judges considered only one meaning of the word periphery, though it had several other meanings which were not considered at all. Such others meanings, he asserted, were more appropriate to decide the question in the facts of the case. According to him, the word 'periphery' meant 'bounding line or surface' 'the outside of anything' 'a surrounding region', vide, Chambers’ Dictionary; 'line round a circle under surface', 'external boundary surface'. The learned Counsel further submitted that the proximity of a hat or bazar does not establish that the plots in question came within the definition of hat or bazar as provided in section 2(12) of the State Acquisition Act and therefore, acquirable under its provisions. 

 "Seen the report of the R.C.O. and the sketch map showing area proposed to be classified as bazar, I personally went to the locality, and personally inspected the area. The area shown in the sketch map in red attested by the R.C.O. and R.V.W. signed by me should be classified bazar and bat area for the purpose of determining' non-retainable khas land under section 20 of the State. Acquisition and Tenancy Act, The S.D.S.O. should finalise the case and the R.C.O. should correct the record accordingly and prepare compensation for the persons concerned."
